short: A neural network design that learns a long-term memory module at test time, updating it most on the most surprising inputs.
definition: Titans is a neural network architecture from Google Research that pairs ordinary attention, used as a short-term memory with limited capacity, with a separate neural long-term memory module whose weights keep updating while the model is running, not just during training. The update is driven by a 'surprise' signal: inputs that most violate what the memory already expects get written in more strongly, while older, less useful memories fade over time. The goal is a model that can effectively make use of far more context than attention alone can handle efficiently, without needing to retrain from scratch to pick up new information.
